blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.text:
The breaking of C – C single bond of complex compounds through oxidation within the cells, leading to release of considerable amounts of energy and the trapping of this energy for synthesis of ATP is called cellular respiration.

Do Plants Breathe?

Plants, unlike animals, have no specialised organs for gaseous exchange but they have stomata and lenticels for this purpose.

blocks.title: Types of Respiration
blocks.text:
(A) ON THE BASIS OF PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF  O₂:

(1) Aerobic

(2) Anaerobic/Fermentation

  • RBC lacks mitochondria, so respire anaerobically

blocks.title: Points To Remember
blocks.text:
• Cellular Respiration: Oxidation of complex compounds to get energy and synthesis of ATP.
  • Respiratory substrate – Carbohydrates (most common), fats, proteins and organic acids.
  • Respiration is an amphibolic process.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Respiration occurs in :-

(1) All living cells both in day and night

(2) Non green cells only in day

(3) Non green cells in both day and night

(4) All living cells in day only
blocks.answer:
Ans= 1

Explanation:

  • Respiration is a continuous metabolic process that occurs in all living cells (both green and non-green cells) to produce energy in the form of ATP.
  • It happens both during the day and night, as energy is required by the cells at all times for various functions like growth, repair, and maintenance.
  • Unlike photosynthesis (which occurs only in green cells and during daylight), respiration is independent of light and takes place continuously.
options: (1) All living cells both in day and night
(2) Non green cells only in day
(3) Non green cells in both day and night
(4) All living cells in day only

blocks.title: Glycolysis
blocks.text:
• In Glycolysis, no consumption of oxygen & no liberation of CO2 takes place.
  • In glycolysis, 1 glucose (6C), break down into 2 mol. of pyruvic acid (3C) (Partial oxidation).
  • Pyruvic acid is the key product of glycolysis.
  • NADH2, produced during the process enter into ETS (In mitochondria) to produce 4ATP (if glycerol phosphate shuttle is present) or 6ATP (if malate aspartate shuttle is present), this ATP formation is called oxidative phosphorylation.
  • Substrate level phosphorylation [When the substrate releases energy for phosphorylation of ADP (formation of ATP) without ETS then this method of ATP formation is called as substrate level phosphorylation], forms 4 ATP, 2ATP consumed, so 2ATP gained by SLP. (Direct gain)

blocks.text:
1. Lactic acid anaerobic respiration: In human muscles (during exercise when oxygen is     inadequate).

2. Alcoholic fermentation: In yeast.

blocks.title: (ii) LINK/GATEWAY REACTION (FORMATION OF ACETYL-CO-A)
blocks.text:
AEROBIC RESPIRATION :

$\text{Pyruvic acid} + \text{CoA} + \text{NAD}^+ \xrightarrow[\text{Pyruvate dehydrogenase}]{\text{Mg}^{2+}} \text{Acetyl CoA} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$

  • During this process 1 st time CO2 is evolved during respiration.
  • Acetyl CoA is a connecting link between glycolysis & Krebs cycle.
  • Decarboxylation and dehydrogenation (Oxidative decarboxylation) takes place during formation of acetyl CoA.
  • Acetyl CoA is formed in the matrix by enzyme pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
  • This reaction require five cofactors. (Mg2+ , LA (Lipoic Acid), TPP (Thiamine pyrophosphate), NAD+ , CoA)
(iii) KREBS CYCLE / TRICARBOXYLIC ACID CYCLE/ CITRIC ACID CYCLE :

blocks.title: Key Points
blocks.text:
• Site of glycolysis – Cytoplasm
  • Site of citric acid cycle – Matrix of mitochondria  Site of ETS – Inner membrane of mitochondria
  • Site of oxidative phosphorylation – Oxysomes/ATP synthase
  • Final electron acceptor is – Oxygen
  • Mobile Electron carrier in ETS is – Cytochrome-C (on the outer surface of inner membrane of mitochondria)
  • Proton accumulation – In inter membrane space.  1NADH = 3ATP, 1FADH2 = 2ATP

blocks.title: Exercise-1
blocks.question:
Fatty acids are connected with the respiratory pathway through:

1. Acetyl CoA

2. Alpha ketoglutaric Acid

3. Dihydroxy acetone phosphate

4. Pyruvic Acid
blocks.answer:
Ans: (1)

Explanation:

  • Fatty acid metabolism involves their breakdown through a process called beta-oxidation in the mitochondria.
  • During beta-oxidation, fatty acids are broken down into two-carbon acetyl groups which combine with coenzyme A to form Acetyl CoA.
  • The resulting Acetyl CoA enters the Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) to participate in the respiratory pathway, producing energy in the form of ATP.

blocks.title: Exercise-2
blocks.question:
How many times decarboxylation occurs during each TCA cycle?

1. Thrice

2. Many

3. Once

4. Twice
blocks.answer:
Ans: (4)

Explanation:

During each turn of the TCA cycle (Krebs cycle), decarboxylation (removal of a CO₂ molecule) occurs twice:

  • First decarboxylation:
  • • Isocitrate is converted to α-ketoglutarate by the enzyme isocitrate dehydrogenase, releasing one CO₂ molecule.
  • Second decarboxylation:
  • • α-ketoglutarate is converted to succinyl-CoA by the enzyme α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, releasing another CO₂ molecule.
Thus, two decarboxylation reactions occur per cycle.

blocks.title: Exercise-3
blocks.question:
What amount of energy is released from glucose during lactic acid fermentation?

1. More than 18%

2. About 10%

3. Less than 7%

4. Approximately 15%
blocks.answer:
Ans: (3)

Explanation:

  • During lactic acid fermentation, glucose is broken down anaerobically to form lactic acid.
  • Only 2 ATP molecules are produced per glucose molecule during this process.
  • The total energy stored in one glucose molecule is approximately 686 kcal/mol.
  • • Each ATP molecule releases about 7.3 kcal of energy.
      • Therefore, the energy captured in 2 ATP is:
2 × 7.3 = 14.6 kcal

blocks.title: Respiratory Quotient: (RQ)
blocks.text:
• The ratio of the volume of CO₂ evolved to the volume of O₂ consumed in respiration is called the respiratory quotient (RQ) or respiratory ratio.
$RQ = \frac{\text{Volume of } CO_2 \text{ evolved}}{\text{Volume of } O_2 \text{ consumed}}$

RQ = 1 (Aerobic respiration)
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O → 6CO₂ + 12H₂O + 686 Kcal kcal

RQ = 6CO₂ / 6O₂ = 1.0

RQ = Less than one :

Eg. When Respiratory substrates are

(i) Proteins RQ = 0.8 or 0.9

(ii) Fats RQ =0 .7

  • RQ = More than 1

blocks.title: Energy efficiency of cellular respiration
blocks.text: $1 \text{ ATP} = 8.1 \text{ Kcal} \\ 1 \text{ Glucose} = 686 \text{ Kcal} \\  \text{If gain is } 36 \text{ ATP then efficiency} = \left(\frac{291.6}{686}\right) \times 100 = 42.50\% \\  \text{If gain is } 38 \text{ ATP then efficiency} = \left(\frac{307.8}{686}\right) \times 100 = 44.86\%$

blocks.title: Exercise-1
blocks.question:
Respiratory Quotient (RQ) value of tripalmitin is:

1. 0.9

2. 0.7

3. 0.07

4. 0.09
blocks.answer:
Ans: (2)

Explanation:

The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) is the ratio of carbon dioxide (CO₂) produced to oxygen (O₂) consumed during the breakdown of a substrate.
